deviations.claim_in_article: “They enjoyed AI’s convenience, but a human was on the other end. They did not realize it.”
deviations.issue: The article presents users’ enjoyment and lack of awareness as events that actually occurred. The Ledger confirms an internal test without appropriate disclosure, but does not establish what the affected users realized or experienced.
deviations.explanation: The definitive claim that users did not realize a human was speaking goes beyond the Ledger’s finding about inadequate disclosure. This is an unsupported new claim and strengthens the certainty of what was observed.
deviations.qualifier_text: “might think”; “If no one explained this clearly”
same_fact_id_locations: If no one explained this clearly, users could not know. They could not tell if it was AI or a person.
Some calls through Meta’s AI assistant were actually handled by humans, but users were not properly told.

deviations.claim_in_article: “It said human staff made inappropriate comments about race during calls. These calls were about trying to lower internet or cable fees.”
deviations.issue: The plural “calls” presents the reported incident as involving multiple calls, while the Ledger describes one reported case.
deviations.explanation: The plural wording expands the scope and number of the Ledger’s single reported case. Attribution to an employee report is retained, but it does not support multiple calls.
deviations.qualifier_text: “one employee’s report”; “However, this is only one report.”
same_fact_id_locations: News reports also cited one employee’s report.
However, this is only one report. It would be wrong to say all contract workers did this.
